p1.original: 12.1 医学模型把心理障碍归为一种“疾病”，而心理学将其视为生物学、行为、认知、发展和社会文化因素相互作用的结果。
p1.en: 12.1 The medical model classifies mental disorders as a “disease”, while psychology sees them as a result of the interplay of biological, behavioural, cognitive, developmental and sociocultural factors.

p2.original: 12.2 DSM-5是使用最广泛的精神障碍分类系统，它根据人的精神和行为症状对精神障碍进行归类。
p2.en: 12.2 DSM-5 is the most widely used classification system for mental disorders, which is classified according to the mental and behavioural symptoms of the person.

p3.original: 12.3 从理论上讲，准确的诊断是做出适当的治疗的前提，但是诊断也可能成为一种标签，使个体失去个性，进而使人们忽视心理问题产生的社会和文化背景。
p3.en: 12.3 In theory, accurate diagnosis is a prerequisite for appropriate treatment, but it can also be a label that deprives individuals of their individuality and thus neglects the social and cultural context in which psychological problems arise.

p4.original: 志愿者们（5位男性和3位女性）知道他们只能靠自己了，如果他们成功入院，就被看作精神病人而非旁观者。尽管这些志愿者没人被诊断出患有精神疾病，但是他们一点也不“正常”：一个正常人会为了要进精神病院而撒谎吗？事实上，这些志愿者是一项实验的合作者，该实验旨在弄清楚精神病院能否识别出正常人。
p4.en: Volunteers (five men and three women) know that they are on their own, and if they succeed, they are seen as mentally ill rather than bystanders. Although none of these volunteers have been diagnosed with mental illness, they are not “normal” at all: would a normal person lie to go to a psychiatric hospital? In fact, the volunteers were co-operatives in an experiment designed to ascertain whether a mental institution could identify a normal person.

p5.original: 实验者大卫·罗森汉（David Rosenhan）也是“伪装病人”之一，他怀疑诸如“心智健全”（sanity）、“精神失常”（insanity）、“精神分裂症”（schizophrenia）、“精神障碍”（mental illness）和“异常”（abnormal）等术语的边界比精神病学界认为的还要模糊。他还怀疑，在精神病人身上出现的一些“异常”行为可能源于精神病院的异常氛围，而不是源自患者本身。为了验证这些想法，罗森汉和他的合作者决定看看医院的专业人员如何处置实际上并没有患精神疾病的患者。他们能区分健康人和精神障碍患者吗？
p5.en: The experimenter, David Rosenhan, is also one of the “disguised patients” who suspects that the boundaries of terms such as “sanity”, “insanity”, “schizophrenia”, “mental disorder” and “abnormal” are more blurred than the psychiatric community believes. He also suspects that some of the “unusual” behaviour in the case of a mentally ill person may originate from the abnormal atmosphere in a psychiatric institution rather than from the patient himself. In order to validate these ideas, Rosenhan and his collaborators decided to see how hospital professionals dealt with patients who were not actually mentally ill. Can they distinguish between healthy people and mentally handicapped people?

p6.original: 志愿者们申请进入不同的医院，他们抱怨最近好像听到了“空虚”“空洞”和“砰砰”之类的声音，除此之外，他们声称没有其他症状。所有人都用了假名，四名心理健康专家（包括罗森汉本人）还伪造了职业，当然，除了这些，他们如实回答了其他所有问题。尽管即将进入陌生的医院环境让他们感到焦虑，但他们还是尽可能地表现正常。实验开始前，他们担心不能被批准入院，也许更糟的是，被人举报欺诈。不过这种担忧很快就消失了，因为所有人很容易就在12家不同的医院获得了住院许可（有些人还获得了两次）。绝大部分人（只有一个人除外）都被诊断患有精神分裂症，这是一种严重的心理障碍，常伴有幻听。
p6.en: The volunteers applied for admission to different hospitals, complaining that they had recently heard “empty” “empty” and “thumping” sounds, with the exception of claims that they had no other symptoms. All used a pseudonym and four mental health specialists (including Rosenham himself) forged a profession, although they answered all the other questions honestly. They are as normal as possible, despite the anxiety they feel about entering a strange hospital environment. Before the experiment began, they feared that they would not be admitted, and perhaps worse, that fraud would be reported. However, this concern quickly disappeared, as it was easy for everyone to obtain hospitalization permits in 12 different hospitals (some have also been granted twice). The vast majority of people (except only one) are diagnosed with schizophrenia, which is a serious psychological disorder, often accompanied by hearing.

p7.original: 在入院之后，这些“伪装病人”就没有再宣称听见声音或存在什么异常症状了。实际情况是，所有人都想好好表现，争取尽快出院。他们仅有的“异常行为”是记录住院经历，起初是私下记录，在发现医护人员没有在意后，开始公开记录。住院记录显示，当医护人员注意到他们的记录行为时，医护人员将此解释为患者疾病的一部分（病历中有一条冷漠的描述是：“病人有记录行为”）。
p7.en: After admission, these “disguised patients” no longer claimed to have heard voices or had any abnormal symptoms. The truth is that everyone wants to do their part and get out of the hospital as soon as possible. Their only “unusual behaviour” was the recording of the hospitalization, initially in private, and began to be made public when medical personnel were found to be unaware. Hospital records show that when medical staff noticed their recorded behaviour, they interpreted it as part of the patient's illness (a cold description in the patient's medical records is “the patient has recorded behaviour”).

p8.original: 很多时候，病人发现，即使他们寻求帮助或建议，医护人员也会忽视他们。当医护人员与他们互动时，病人好像也只是“病例”，而不是活生生的人。因此，在没有异常症状出现的情况下，这些“伪装病人”要让医护人员相信自己可以出院，大概平均需要19天的时间。一名运气不好的志愿者在两个月后才被医院“释放”。
p8.en: In many cases, patients find that even if they seek help or advice, they are ignored by health-care personnel. When medical personnel interact with them, it also seems that patients are “cases”, not living people. Therefore, in the absence of abnormal symptoms, these “disguised patients” take about 19 days on average to convince medical staff that they can be discharged. One of the unlucky volunteers was “released” from the hospital two months later.

p9.original: 这项经典研究的主要发现让精神病学界大为震惊。
p9.en: The main findings of this classic study have shocked the psychiatry community.

p10.original: 首先，没有任何一家医院的专业人士意识到罗森汉的伪装病人是在假装患有精神疾病。
p10.en: First, no hospital professional is aware that Rosenham's disguised patient is pretending to be suffering from mental illness.

p11.original: 当然，工作人员可能认为病人在入院时确实是生病的，在住院期间病情有所好转。但这种解释没有让罗森汉放弃对他们的指责：尽管伪装病人们行为正常，但在医院中，工作人员并不认为他们“健康”或“正常”。哪怕出院后，工作人员也仍然认为他们患有精神分裂症，只不过是处于缓解期。
p11.en: Of course, staff may believe that the patient was indeed ill at the time of admission and that the condition improved during hospitalization. But this interpretation did not allow Rosenhan to abandon the blame on them: although the patients were acting normally, they were not considered “healthy” or “normal” by the staff at the hospital. Even after their release, staff members continued to believe that they were suffering from schizophrenia, which was merely in a palliative phase.

p12.original: 医院的工作人员是没水平还是没感情
p12.en: Does the hospital staff have no quality or no feelings?

p13.original: 罗森汉没有贸然下结论。他指出，工作人员没有意识到这些人是伪装病人这件事很正常，因为这些工作人员整天忙于文案和其他工作，几乎没有时间观察病人以及与病人交流。医院的环境设计也催生了这个问题：工作人员大部分时间都待在一间玻璃围住的中央办公室里，病人称之为“笼子”。正如罗森汉自己所说（Rosenhan，1973a）：
p13.en: Rosenhan didn't come to a quick conclusion. He pointed out that it was normal for staff members not to realize that they were disguised patients, as they were engaged in paperwork and other work all day and had little time to observe and communicate with patients. The environmental design of the hospital has also given rise to this problem: staff members spend most of their time in a glass-conveneed central office, referred to by patients as “cages”. As Rosenhan himself said:

p14.original: 如果认为发生在我们身上的事情是由于工作人员的恶意或愚蠢造成的，这可能是一个错误，而且是非常不应该的错误。相反，他们给我们留下了深刻印象，他们关心病人、有责任感，也非常睿智。他们没有意识到伪装病人的正常行为，将这些失误归因于他们所处的环境比归因于个体的麻木不仁会更准确。他们的感知和行为受到了情境的控制。
p14.en: It may be a mistake, and it is a very wrong mistake, to think that what happened to us was caused by the malice or foolishness of the staff. On the contrary, they have impressed us by their caring, responsible and very wise attitude towards the sick. They were not aware of the normal behaviour of the disguised patients, and it would be more accurate to attribute these errors to the circumstances in which they were found than to the insensitiveness attributed to the individual. Their perception and behaviour are controlled by circumstances.

p15.original: 有没有可能伪装病人困在医院里时，行为并不像他们想象中的那么正常？罗森汉指出：出乎所有人的意料，尽管专业人员没有发现病人是伪装的，但医院里的其他病人很容易就发现了其中的问题。伪装病人报告说，其他病人经常会提出质疑：“你不是疯子。你是记者或者教授……你在调查医院。”罗森汉（1973a）在题为“在精神失常的地方保持神志正常”（On Being Sane in Insane Places）的报告中客观地指出：“重要的是，常常是病人们发现了医院里的正常人，而医生却没有发现。”你将在贯穿本章的问题中找到对这些“重要问题”的回应。
p15.en: Is it possible that when patients are trapped in hospitals, they don't behave as normal as they think? Rosenhan noted that, to the surprise of all, although professionals did not find the patient disguised, other patients in the hospital could easily discover the problem. The masked patient reports that other patients often question: “You're not crazy. You're a journalist or a professor... you're investigating the hospital. “On Being Sane in Insane Places” (1973a) states objectively: “It is often the sick who find normal people in the hospital, and the doctors do not. “You will find responses to these `important issues' in the issues that cut across this chapter.

p16.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p17.original: 能不能区分精神障碍和单纯的行为异常？即是否有明确证据证明精神障碍的存在？
p17.en: Can you distinguish between mental disorders and simple behaviour abnormalities? Is there clear evidence of mental disorders?

p18.original: 罗森汉的研究引发了巨大的轰动，许多精神病学家和临床心理学家都表示严重抗议。发表该研究成果的期刊《科学》（Science）随后发表了几篇回应文章，指责罗森汉的研究粗制滥造，损害了精神健康专业人员的声誉。这样的回应有道理吗？罗森汉的研究有缺陷吗？或者他们的反应仅仅是那些职业自尊心受到伤害的人的呐喊？值得注意的是，罗森汉并不否认心理障碍的存在，他质疑的是在精神病院的环境下做出的临床诊断。时至今日，他的研究仍然有意义，因为他的发现，医生们一直致力于优化精神障碍的诊断流程。
p18.en: The research in Rosenhan has generated a great deal of excitement, with serious protests from a number of psychiatrists and clinical psychologists. The journal Science, which published the results of the study, subsequently published several articles in response, accusing Rosenham of being crude in research, damaging the reputation of mental health professionals. Is that a reasonable response? Is there a flaw in Rosenham's research? Or are they just responding to the cries of those whose professional self-esteem is hurt? It is worth noting that Rosenhan does not deny the existence of mental disorders and that he questions the clinical diagnosis made in the context of a psychiatric institution. His research remains relevant to this day because of his findings that doctors have been working to optimize the diagnostic process of mental disorders.

p19.original: 事实上，数以百万计的人确实经历过精神病理学（psychopathology）意义上的病痛（亦称为精神障碍或精神疾病）。根据美国精神卫生研究所（NIMH，2010b）的数据，超26%（即超1/4）的美国人，会在某一年被诊断有精神健康问题。每17人中就有1人患有严重的精神疾病，如重性抑郁症（major depression）或精神分裂症（schizophrenia）。在美国，估计46%的人会被诊断出某种形式的心理障碍（Butcher et al.，2008）。在下面的部分，我们会探讨构成心理障碍的关键问题。
p19.en: In fact, millions of people have experienced the pain (also known as mental disorder or mental illness) in the sense of psychophysics (psychophatic). According to the American Institute of Mental Health (NIMH, 2010b), over 26 per cent (i.e. over one quarter) of Americans are diagnosed with mental health problems in a given year. One in 17 persons suffers from serious mental illness, such as severe depression (major depression) or schizophrenia. In the United States, an estimated 46 per cent of the population is diagnosed with some form of mental disorder (Butcher et al., 2008). In the following section, we will address the key issues that constitute psychological barriers.
